SALES-CTX-G2.title: Trellis Flow competitive battlecard and field FAQ
SALES-CTX-G2.text:
TRELLIS FLOW - COMPETITIVE BATTLECARD AND FIELD FAQ
Corvane Systems sales enablement. Updated 12 August 2026. Internal use only.

READ THIS FIRST
Competitor information comes from win/loss calls, public web pages and what prospects tell us. It can be wrong or out of date. Never quote a competitor's price or security status to a prospect as fact. Say what we know about ourselves and suggest the prospect asks the competitor directly.

PAYLANE
Typical quote reported by prospects for around 10,000 invoices a month: $3,100 to $3,400 a month (unverified).
Strengths: quick setup (2 to 3 weeks reported), a good mobile approval app, very comfortable for QuickBooks-only companies.
Gaps we have seen: two-way matching only with no configurable three-way tolerance rules; no EU data residency; SOC 2 Type I at last check; no SAP connector.
We tend to win: multi-entity companies, purchase-order-heavy buying, SAP or NetSuite with custom fields, EU data needs.
We tend to lose: small teams with simple non-PO invoices that choose on price.
Guidance: do not disparage. Ask which matching rules the prospect needs, then let them compare.

BOOKWISE AP
Typical quote for 10,000 invoices a month: about $5,800 a month plus a $20,000 implementation (unverified).
Strengths: long ERP list including Workday, very deep audit trail.
Gaps: implementations of 16 to 20 weeks reported, and per-user pricing that gets expensive with many approvers.
We tend to win: prospects who must be live within a quarter, and companies with hundreds of occasional approvers.

APPROVED TALKING POINTS
Price: Growth at 10,000 invoices a month works out to $0.48 per invoice in subscription fees, against a customer-reported median manual cost of $11.40 per invoice. Do not promise savings to a specific prospect before we have seen their volumes.
Security: the SOC 2 Type II report can be shared under NDA. ISO 27001 is in progress and not yet certified. Say exactly that.
NetSuite: custom fields are mapped through a mapping table configured in week 2 of implementation. The Business Central connector is in beta; production use needs Solutions Engineering sign-off.
Migration: vendor master, open purchase orders and historical bills are imported by CSV or API in 5 to 7 business days. We recommend a two-week parallel run and cutover at the start of a month, so the customer does not have to stop processing invoices.
References: up to two, after NDA, same industry when possible. We do not publish customer names.

WHO WE NEED FROM THE CUSTOMER
A finance owner (about 4 hours a week during implementation), an IT contact with ERP admin rights (about 10 hours in total), and the AP lead. Go-live dates are only committed after a technical scoping call.

WHAT WE DO NOT DO
No custom development on Growth. No on-premise hosting. No guaranteed savings figure.

SALES-CTX-G1.title: Trellis Flow one-pager and pricing and packaging sheet (rev 4.1)
SALES-CTX-G1.text:
CORVANE SYSTEMS - TRELLIS FLOW
Product one-pager and pricing and packaging sheet, revision 4.1, effective 1 September 2026.

WHAT IT IS
Trellis Flow automates accounts payable for mid-market finance teams. It captures vendor invoices from email, PDF upload or EDI, extracts the fields, matches them against purchase orders and receipts, routes exceptions for approval, and posts approved bills to the ERP. Target customer: 100 to 2,000 employees, 1,500 to 40,000 invoices a month, finance team of 3 to 25 people.

HEADLINE RESULTS
Customer-reported medians across 41 customers live for at least six months. Corvane has not independently audited these figures.
- Cost per processed invoice down 63 percent (from $11.40 to about $4.20)
- Approval cycle time down from 4.1 days to 1.6 days
- Touchless rate (invoices posted with no human touch) 71 percent at month six
Customer references are available only after a mutual NDA is signed. Corvane does not publish customer names.

PLANS (monthly list price, billed annually in advance)
Starter: $1,900 a month. Up to 2,000 invoices a month, 1 entity, 10 users, QuickBooks Online and Xero connectors, email support, 99.5 percent uptime target. No SSO.
Growth: $4,800 a month. Up to 10,000 invoices a month, up to 3 entities, 40 users, NetSuite and QuickBooks Online connectors, Dynamics 365 Business Central connector (beta), SAML SSO, two-way and three-way matching, 99.9 percent uptime SLA, business-hours support with 4-hour first response.
Enterprise: from $14,500 a month, quoted per deal. More than 10,000 invoices a month, unlimited entities, SAP S/4HANA connector (generally available), SCIM provisioning, EU data residency (Frankfurt), 99.95 percent uptime SLA, named customer success manager, 24x7 support with 1-hour first response for severity 1 issues.
Overage: $0.85 per invoice above the plan limit on Starter and Growth. Enterprise overage is set in the order form.

IMPLEMENTATION (one-time fee)
Starter: self-serve, $0. Growth: $12,000 fixed fee, typically 6 weeks from kickoff to go-live. Enterprise: from $38,000, typically 10 to 14 weeks. Data migration (vendor master, open purchase orders, historical bills by CSV or API) takes 5 to 7 business days and is included in the fee. A Workday Financials connector is on the roadmap for Q2 2027 and is not a commitment.

DISCOUNTS AND COMMERCIAL TERMS
- Annual prepay is the list price basis. Monthly billing costs 10 percent more.
- Multi-year: 2-year term 10 percent off, 3-year term 15 percent off, applied to subscription only, never to implementation fees.
- Sales reps may approve up to 10 percent total discount. Anything above 10 percent needs Deal Desk approval. Discounts above 20 percent are not offered.
- Standard payment terms are net 30. Net 45 needs Deal Desk approval. Net 60 is not offered. Quarterly billing is available on Growth and Enterprise with a 3 percent surcharge.
- Default term is 12 months, auto-renews for 12 months, 60 days' written notice to cancel. Renewal increases are capped at 5 percent.
- No termination for convenience. Termination for cause with a 30-day cure period.
- Corvane liability is capped at 12 months of fees. Uncapped liability is not offered. On Enterprise only, a data breach super-cap of 2x annual fees is negotiable.

PROOF OF VALUE
There is no self-serve free trial. Qualified Growth and Enterprise prospects can run a 30-day proof of value in a sandbox using up to 500 of their own historical invoices at no charge. It requires a signed evaluation agreement and one named technical contact.

SECURITY AND COMPLIANCE
SOC 2 Type II (most recent report period ended 31 March 2026). ISO 27001 certification is in progress with a target of Q1 2027; Corvane is not yet certified. AES-256 encryption at rest, TLS 1.2 or higher in transit. Data is hosted in the US by default; EU residency (Frankfurt) is Enterprise only. Annual third-party penetration test, summary available under NDA. No security incident requiring customer notification since launch in 2021.

FSALES-CTX-G1.title: Harborline Cold Chain Monitor pricing and hardware sheet
FSALES-CTX-G1.text:
Harborline Cold Chain Monitor - Pricing and Hardware Sheet 2026
Harborline Systems | Rep and partner use | Effective 1 February 2026

WHAT IT DOES
Harborline Cold Chain Monitor watches refrigerated storage and transport for food distributors, commissaries and grocery warehouses. Wireless sensors report to a gateway, the gateway reports to the Harborline cloud, and the cloud alerts staff when a reading leaves the allowed band and builds audit-ready logs.

Measured signals: temperature, door-open events, gateway connectivity and sensor battery level. Nothing else is measured today.

HARDWARE (one-time, customer owns the hardware once paid)
- HL-T3 wireless temperature sensor: $89 each. Range -40 C to +85 C, accuracy +/-0.3 C. Each unit ships with a NIST-traceable calibration certificate valid for 24 months.
- HL-D1 door-open sensor: $45 each.
- HL-G2 gateway (Wi-Fi or Ethernet): $340 each. One gateway covers up to 60 sensors within about 100 m indoors.
- HL-G2C cellular gateway for trucks and trailers: $520 each, includes 24 months of cellular data; after that $9 per gateway per month.
- Replacement battery pack: $12. Batteries are user-replaceable.

BATTERY LIFE (HL-T3)
- 10-minute logging interval (default): about 3 years.
- 1-minute logging interval: about 18 months.
Battery life drops in freezers below -25 C; plan on roughly 20% shorter life there.

SUBSCRIPTION (per HL-T3 sensor per month, billed annually)
- Standard: $6 per sensor per month. Email and push alerts, dashboards, 7-year log history, PDF temperature logs.
- Premium: $9 per sensor per month. Adds SMS and automated voice-call alerts, escalation chains and 24/7 alert support.
- Volume pricing at 250+ sensors on one contract: Standard $5, Premium $7.50 per sensor per month.
- Door sensors are $2 per door sensor per month on either plan. Gateways carry no subscription fee.

INSTALLATION
- Remote-guided self-install: free, with a 60-minute video session.
- On-site installation: $1,200 per site for up to 150 sensors, plus $6 per additional sensor at that site.
- Installation fee waivers are not pre-approved; route any request to the regional sales manager in writing.

LEAD TIME AND SHIPPING
- 3 to 4 weeks from purchase order for orders under 500 sensors; larger orders are quoted individually.
- Ships to the United States and Canada.

PILOT PROGRAM
- 45-day pilot: up to 25 sensors and 1 gateway, $1,500 flat.
- The $1,500 is credited in full against the first-year subscription if the customer signs within 30 days of the pilot ending.
- Pilot hardware can be kept if the customer signs; otherwise it is returned prepaid.

RULES FOR REPS
Quote list prices only. Discounts beyond the volume tier need regional sales manager approval. Do not quote battery life beyond the figures above.

items.answer: I'd keep it simple and flattering: tell them the logo work is exactly what we want more of, and that's why I want to size it properly before it goes in the forecast. Then ask what budget they've set aside and who signs off, so we both know if this is a quick yes or a longer build. That way they hear interest, not doubt.

items.question: What can I trade instead of price?
conversation: USER (typed to Natively): They want a twenty-five percent discount and I can only approve ten. What are my options?

NATIVELY: I can do ten percent today, and I want to be straight with you rather than bounce this around. If the number has to land closer to twenty-five, the lever I'd pull is scope or term, not the rate. What's driving the twenty-five, budget or a competing quote?
items.answer: Ten percent is what I can approve today. Beyond that, I'd rather trade than cut the rate: a longer term, a smaller scope, or a case study and referral I can point to. Which of those actually matters on your side?

items.answer: I can't quote Paylane's price or their security status as fact, so let me tell you what we know about ourselves and where we genuinely differ. The two gaps that usually matter are configurable three-way tolerance rules on matching, and EU data residency, and we're SOC 2 Type II with the report shareable under NDA. If your invoices are simple and non-PO, Paylane is a fair choice and I'd rather you pick right than pick us. Which matching rules do you actually need?

items.answer: Good catch, and sorry for the confusion. The list shows the HL-G2 at **$290**, but that same list notes the price moves to **$340** effective 1 July. So if you're buying now, budget 290, and 340 for anything after that date. Which timeline are you working toward?

items.question: Can you explain in a sentence what Trellis Flow actually does?
items.answer: Trellis Flow automates accounts payable for mid-market finance teams: it captures vendor invoices from email, PDF or EDI, extracts the fields, matches them against purchase orders and receipts, routes exceptions for approval, and posts approved bills to the ERP. In short, it takes invoices from inbox to ERP with as little human touch as possible.

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: How does implementation usually go with a company our size?
items.answer:
For a team your size, implementation is usually pretty light. We'd start with a short kickoff to map your current setup, then run the rollout in stages so nothing disrupts your day-to-day, and I'd stay hands-on through the first few weeks until your team is comfortable. Most of the work sits on our side, not yours.

What does your team's setup look like today, so I can tell you exactly what those stages would be for you?

items.role: USER: the seller / account executive. OTHER PARTY: the prospect / customer. Natively: words the seller can say next (or private help when the seller types).
items.question: What if it fails?
conversation: PROSPECT (heard): We're looking at a few vendors, and frankly whoever's cheapest is probably going to win.

NATIVELY: Cheapest is a fair place to start, and I'd rather you compare on total cost than sticker price, because the cheap option usually shows up later in implementation time and support. Can I ask what's driving the budget pressure, and what the number needs to cover? If I know that, I can show you where we land on value rather than just price.
PROSPECT (heard): Why pay more?

NATIVELY: Because the cheapest quote is usually the smallest part of what you actually pay. What I'd want you to weigh is what happens after go-live: how fast issues get fixed, how much of your team's time it eats, and what it costs to switch if it doesn't work. If price is the deciding factor, tell me the number it has to hit and I'll show you honestly where we can and can't get there.
items.answer: If it fails, you're not stuck with it. What I'd want you to know before you sign is how we handle it: how fast we respond when something breaks, what it takes to get you back up, and what it costs you to walk away if we can't fix it. Can I walk you through that, and what would a failure look like on your side?

What I can tell you is that pricing depends on how much of the quoting process we're automating and how many systems we're connecting, so the range moves a lot. items.question: Everyone says automation saves time. What does that actually mean in dollars for a company like ours?
items.answer: It means hours back, and hours have a rate. If a team of ten spends a day a week on something a tool can do, that's roughly a fifth of their capacity, and at a loaded cost of, say, eighty dollars an hour, that's real money every month. The honest number comes from your own time logs, not a generic benchmark. What's the process you'd most want to take off their plate first?

items.question: We'd be looking at about three hundred and twenty temperature sensors across two warehouses, plus our eleven trucks. Ballpark, what's year one with hardware, and how do the trucks connect?
items.answer:
Let's do the math out loud. Three hundred and twenty sensors at **$89** each is **$28,480**, and the gateways run about **$2,040** for the warehouses, six of them at $340 to cover 320 sensors at 60 per gateway. For the eleven trucks, a cellular gateway each at $520 is **$5,720**, and that includes 24 months of data. So hardware lands around **$36,240** before any door sensors or installation.

On subscription, 320 sensors puts you over the 250 threshold, so Standard is $5 per sensor per month, which is **$19,200** for year one. The trucks connect through the HL-G2C cellular gateway, one per truck, reporting straight to the cloud over cellular with no Wi-Fi needed.

Want me to put this on paper as a formal quote, or start with a 45-day pilot on one warehouse first?
